Here, we integrate single nucleus RNA-seq and single-cell ATAC sequencing data generated from germinal matrix and cortical plate regions macrodissected from prenatal and postnatal developing brain autopsy tissue, creating an expanded spatiotemporal multi-omic dataset of gliogenic progenitors. The integrated multi-omics data includes previously published data (Ramos et al, Nature Commun 2022; Herring et al, Cell 2022) as well as newly-generated and herein deposited data. We use this dataset to interrogate oncofetal cell state composition in grade 4 gliomas across several published high-grade glioma / glioblastoma (GBM) datasets to uniquely assess tumor heterogeneity related to infiltrative biology near the margin and disease recurrence, in addition to genomic drivers. Our analyses reveal the preferential enrichment of glial intermediate progenitor cell (gIPC)-like cell state in GBM, most reminiscent of third-trimester germinal matrix gIPC progenitors, across tumor regions and in recurrence, irrespective of EGFR amplification status.

metadata.summary: Microexons are extremely short exons that are highly conserved in vertebrates and are essential for normal brain development. Their small size poses a challenge for canonical exon-definition splice site recognition, which typically relies on spliceosomal interactions across standard length exons. Here, we determine the sequence and RNA structural features of neural microexons in humans in comparison with chickens. We find that neural microexons share intronic features that extend the functional distance between the branchpoint and the 3’ splice site, including distal positioning and lengthening of polypyrimidine tracts. Using experimental RNA structure-probing on a subset of neural microexons, we show that the branchpoint-to-splice site region is unusually accessible and relatively unpaired compared to other exon classes. However, we find little support for shared RNA secondary structures between orthologous human and chicken precursor RNAs despite high sequence conservation. Using the chick embryo as a developmental model, we demonstrate that a subset of neural microexons undergo dynamic, stage-specific regulation during brain development that correlates with expression of known microexon regulators, SRRM4 and NOVA1. Our data suggest that neural microexon splicing fluctuates during brain development and may rely on an extended polypyrimidine tract and structural accessibility for splicing efficiency, rather than conserved secondary structures.

observations.text: Systematically perturbing neuronal circuits under controlled conditions offers a promising route to understanding how they encode and process information, yet remains methodologically demanding. In vitro neuronal networks can be cultured on microelectrode arrays (MEAs) that allow stimulation and recording, and microfluidic patterning can constrain network topology to yield stable stimulation-evoked responses. Yet, the space of possible spatiotemporal stimulation patterns remains too large for exhaustive exploration. Additionally, the evoked responses depend on prior stimulation history. Here, we present an open-source framework that sustains closed-loop reinforcement-learning (RL) control of engineered neuronal networks, sending electrical stimuli to the MEA and evaluating the evoked responses to identify stimulation patterns that drive specific target activity motifs. We extend inkube, a low-cost, open-source electrophysiology system from off-the-shelf components, with closed-loop electrophysiology. This enables reliable delivery of stimulation at single-sample precision with millisecond-range round-trip times. It also allows independent RL agents to control multiple networks simultaneously. As a proof-of-principle application, we benchmarked different agents on the task of identifying stimulation patterns that maximise the length of clockwise-circular firing sequences. We first demonstrated that stimulation-evoked responses in engineered recurrent networks were stable and separable across the action space over hours of continuous operation. We characterised the dependency of responses on prior stimulation history, finding state dependence in a subset of stimulus pairs. The agents learned to improve reward during training with respect to random stimulation. Agents converged on non-trivial stimulation patterns that span the full action space rather than mirroring the target motif. All hardware designs and software are publicly available, providing an accessible platform for goal-directed functional characterisation of engineered neuronal networks at single-spike resolution.

observations.text: Cardiac development involves extensive metabolic remodeling, yet dynamic changes of endogenous lipid species during human cardiomyocyte (CM) differentiation remain poorly characterized. In this study, we systematically performed high-coverage lipidomic profiling across five consecutive CM differentiation stages, using high-performance liquid chromatography. MYL2 expression confirmed ventricular lineage specification in late-stage CMs. Ceramide levels peaked at the cardiac progenitor cell (CPC) stage, suggesting a stage-specific association with the mesendoderm (MES)-to-CPC transition. Meanwhile, lipid categories such as monosialodihexosylganglioside, phosphatidylcholine (PC), lysophosphatidylcholine, and lysophosphatidic acid were markedly elevated in mature CMs. Integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility analyses further delineated the temporal regulatory landscape underlying stage-dependent lipid remodeling during cardiogenic differentiation. Functional assays revealed that PC promotes the expression of mature CM marker genes and improves the CM viability. Collectively, these findings establish a comprehensive, high-resolution dynamic lipidomic atlas of in vitro hESC-derived CM differentiation, providing a valuable resource for understanding lipid-associated mechanism in heart development.

observations.text: Open chromatin regions (OCRs) delineate cell-type-specific regulatory landscapes across the genome, yet their functional importance varies considerably. Here, we introduce CAMBUS (Chromatin Accessibility Mutation Burden Score), a machine-learning framework that quantifies the sensitivity of predicted chromatin accessibility to sequence perturbation to prioritize functionally important OCRs. Applying CAMBUS to 29 immune cell types, we identified 66,043 CAMBUS-defined OCRs (cOCRs), without directly incorporating human genetic variation or existing evolutionary constraint metrics. Nevertheless, cOCRs were strongly enriched in independently defined constrained regions (odds ratio (OR)=11.45 (95% confidence interval (CI) 9.33-14.05), P=4.7 x 10-68), and active regulatory elements, with enrichment for super-enhancers remaining after adjustment for established constraint metrics and sequence features (OR=6.18 (95% CI 3.80-10.05), P=2.1 x 10-13). cOCRs also showed cell-type-specific enrichment for the heritability of immune-mediated diseases and for putative causal variants identified by statistical fine-mapping across European and East Asian ancestries, including rare variants. Integration with statistical fine-mapping further linked 1,533 putative causal variants across 70 complex traits to cell-type-specific cOCRs, revealing plausible regulatory mechanisms underlying complex traits. Together, CAMBUS provides a region-centered framework for identifying regulatory elements whose predicted activity is sensitive to sequence disruption and that are enriched for evolutionary constraint, complementing existing regulatory and constraint annotations for interpreting non-coding genetic variation.
observations.title: Sequence sensitivity of open chromatin reveals constrained regulatory elements underlying human traits

metadata.summary: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on a combination of canonical cardiac transcription factors, typically consisting of Mef2c, Gata4, and Tbx5 (MGT). However, successful lineage conversion requires additional endogenous factors that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional changes underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (Atf7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. Loss of function studies in primary murine cardiac fibroblasts demonstrate that Atf7 knockdown markedly reduces MGT mediated reprogramming efficiency, with the strongest impairment occurring when Atf7 is depleted during the early priming window of days 0–3. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that Atf7 knockdown disrupts the induction of cardiomyocyte gene programs while derepressing fibroblast  and extracellular matrix–associated pathways, shifting the global expression profile toward a non reprogrammed state. These findings support a bifunctional regulatory role of Atf7 in promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation while repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks.

metadata.summary: Myocardial infarction (MI) causes cardiomyocyte loss and fibrotic scar formation, disrupting electrical communication and impairing cardiac function. Conductive hydrogels have been studied to reconstruct an electroactive microenvironment for the infarcted myocardium, yet their regenerative effect is limited by the impaired function of surviving cardiomyocytes. Here, we developed a mechanoelectrically active and paintable hydrogel capable of converting cardiac motion into localized electrical stimulation to repair infarcted myocardium. The paintable nature of the hydrogel enables easy application onto irregular epicardial surfaces using a customized brush, while subsequent photocrosslinking allows selective adhesion of the hydrogel to only epicardial surfaces, not to surrounding tissues. Under cyclic loading and in contracting cardiac organoids, the hydrogel generated physiologically relevant electrical potentials, demonstrating efficient deformation-induced charge generation. In a rat MI model, the hydrogel providing electrostimulation alleviated ventricular wall thinning and fibrosis, promoted neovascularization and M2 macrophage polarization, and improved cardiac function. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed upregulation of genes involved in myocardial contraction and energy metabolism. As such, our study offers a minimally invasive and clinically translatable approach for cardiac repair and other tissue applications.

BackgroundGirls are more likely than boys to experience psychological distress during adolescence. Drivers of this gender gap remain under-studied, despite its large impact on later life and outcomes, especially for women. Explanatory factors can be gendered in their prevalence (differential exposure) and/or in their impact (differential susceptibility). We developed a multi-domain framework of explanatory factors for distress and applied it in four low- and middle-income countries.

MethodsWe first proposed a framework of explanatory factors for psychological distress grouped into seven domains (biological, cognitive, psychological, behavioural, social, environmental and broader societal). We applied this framework to identify explanatory variables assessed in childhood and adolescence in the Young Lives longitudinal cohort studies in Ethiopia (N=908), India (N=952), Peru (N=634) and Vietnam (N=887). Distress symptoms at 18-19 years were measured with the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire Emotional Symptoms scale. Gendered prevalence of each explanatory factor was tested with Mann-Whitney tests, and gendered impact with country-specific linear regressions including a gender-by-factor interaction term. Exploratory boosted-tree machine-learning models, interpreted with SHAP values and permutation feature importance, examined the contribution of these factors to the gender gap in each country.

ResultsDistress was higher in girls than boys in every country, the gap ranging from 0.62 points in Ethiopia and Vietnam to 1.76 in India and 2.45 in Peru. Some explanatory factors were consistently gendered in prevalence (e.g. girls experienced greater role overload in each country), while others were gendered only in some countries (e.g. study amount was higher for girls in Peru and Vietnam, but not Ethiopia or India). Gendered impacts on distress displayed more variability across countries. For example, higher self-esteem was more protective for boys than girls in India, Peru and Vietnam, but more protective for girls in Ethiopia. The machine-learning models identified important predictors across all framework domains, though their salience varied by country.

ConclusionsOur findings underscore the importance of considering multi-domain explanations for mental-health outcomes and observed inequalities in mental health. Large cross-country differences in the gender gap and in the prevalence and influence of explanatory factors caution against generalising drivers of mental-health outcomes and inequalities across contexts.
observations.title: Why are girls more distressed than boys? A multi-domain framework applied to longitudinal data across four countries

BackgroundEmergency department (ED) triage is a decision process that determines patient prioritization and resource allocation. Large language models (LLMs) have been proposed as decision-support tools for triage, yet most evaluations rely on curated datasets. Evidence from real-world clinical environments remains limited. The objective of this project was to evaluate the performance and reproducibility of multiple contemporary large language models for Emergency Severity Index (ESI) classification and sectoral allocation (ED vs. urgent care practice, UCP) using a real-world triage dataset.

Material and MethodsRetrospective cross-sectional benchmarking study conducted at a tertiary academic ED in Germany with an integrated central point of assessment (CPA). The study included all 16,107 walk-in encounters between October 18, 2023, and February 27, 2024. Sixteen configurations were compared on the first 2,000 encounters; GPT 5.1 with high reasoning effort was additionally evaluated on all 16,107 encounters. Data were collected from a structured clinical decision support system capturing presenting complaints, vital signs, and triage decisions recorded by specialized nursing staff.

ResultsThe primary outcome was the agreement between LLM-predicted and nurse-assigned ESI levels measured using quadratic-weighted Cohens {kappa}. Secondary outcomes included sectoral assignment agreement, misclassification patterns (over- and under-triage), confidence-agreement comparisons, and output reproducibility. In the primary analysis of all 16,107 encounters, GPT 5.1 with high reasoning effort achieved quadratic-weighted {kappa} = 0.5031 (95% CI 0.4904-0.5158). In the exploratory comparison of 16 configurations on the shared 2,000-encounter subset, quadratic-weighted {kappa} ranged from 0.180 to 0.860. The Stepwise approach, combining structured model assessments with deterministic ESI mapping, achieved {kappa}_qw = 0.860 (95% CI 0.841-0.878) and 82.70% exact agreement. Most models demonstrated moderate or lower agreement. Sectoral assignment agreement (i.e. ED vs. urgent care practice, UCP) was uniformly low ({kappa} [≤] 0.304). Reproducibility testing revealed substantial variability in 23% of cases, indicating non-deterministic output behavior for clinically relevant decisions.

ConclusionsCurrent large language models demonstrate heterogeneous and generally limited performance in real-world emergency triage tasks. The Stepwise approach achieved the highest agreement. Before clinical implementation, confidence estimates, reliability, and workflow integration require prospective validation in regulatory-compliant clinical settings.

observations.text: Leveraging its non-invasive and convenient nature, urinary cytology offers a way for the early diagnosis and surveillance of bladder cancer (BCa). However, its sensitivity remains substantially inferior to the histopathological gold standard, rendering it inadequate to support precise clinical diagnosis. Here, we developed Lipid-featured Urine Cytology with Intelligent Detection (LUCID), an automated platform integrating single-cell stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) imaging and explainable AI model for accurate BCa detection. Following a newly developed standardized urine-preprocessing protocol, 19,678 urinary exfoliated cells from 26 BCa patients and 54 non-BCa participants were imaged using two-color SRS microscopy to simultaneously visualize lipid and protein distributions. For cell-level analysis, a customized deep-supervised Cellpose segmentation algorithm and a YOLO-based detection model were developed to enable precise single-cell segmentation and intracellular lipid droplet (LD) identification, respectively. Totally 20 quantitative morphological and compositional features per cell were extracted and 10 related principal components were obtained via principal component analysis. These features were subsequently integrated into a multiple-instance learning (MIL)-XGBoosting model, which achieved robust diagnostic performance, with 92.31% sensitivity, 87.04% specificity, and an AUC of 0.940. We found that morphological and compositional features provided complementary diagnostic information, while LD-associated features provided primary discriminative information, supporting intracellular LD phenotypes as potential urinary cellular markers of BCa. More importantly, LUCID demonstrated exceptional accuracy in detecting early-stage and small tumors, and showed higher concordance than FISH in a preliminary paired subset (5/6 vs. 2/6). Together, LUCID establishes a chemical imaging-AI paradigm that transforms molecular urine cytology.

metadata.summary: Non-infectious granulomatous diseases, including sarcoidosis, lack targeted, steroid-sparing therapies to disrupt the persistent immune cell aggregates that drive chronic tissue morbidity. Integrating multi-organ single-cell RNA sequencing with spatial transcriptomics, we identify conserved macrophage-specific induction of osteopontin (OPN) across human skin, lung, and heart lesions. Mechanistically, we show that local tissue coagulation acts as a functional checkpoint, where proteolytic cleavage of OPN by tissue thrombin generates OPN fragments that activate macrophages through α4 integrin, which amplifies macrophage OPN expression and establishes a feed-forward circuit that sustains granuloma stability. In mouse models, genetic or pharmacologic disruption of this coagulation-immune axis, including the repurposed direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran and thrombin cleavage-blocking OPN antibodies, reduces granuloma formation and promotes resolution of established chronic lesions. Together, these findings identify a thrombin-dependent feed-forward coagulation–immune circuit that maintains granuloma stability and provides multiple therapeutically actionable targets for non-infectious granulomatous disease.

metadata.summary: Truncating variants in desmoplakin (DSP) are a leading cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a severe heart muscle disease characterized by fibrosis and life-threatening arrhythmias. Desmoplakin anchors the junctions that hold heart muscle cells together to the internal cytoskeleton, enabling the heart to withstand the force of each contraction. No targeted therapy exists, and DSP is too large for conventional gene replacement. Here we show, in explanted human hearts and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, that truncating DSP variants reduce desmoplakin RNA and protein, and that the resulting haploinsufficiency renders cardiomyocytes vulnerable to cell–cell adhesion failure under contractile stress, preceded by disruption of the cell membrane. Lowering contractile force with the myosin inhibitor mavacamten prevents this failure. Circumventing the size of DSP, CRISPR-based transcriptional activation of the endogenous gene restores desmoplakin expression and rescues adhesion. Haploinsufficiency is therefore the primary defect in DSP cardiomyopathy, and transcriptional activation offers a therapeutic strategy.

metadata.summary: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury triggers the recruitment of inflammatory cells, including neutrophils and monocytes. Currently, effective treatment strategies are not available for this widely occurring harmful condition. Using metabololipidomics, we uncovered relative reductions in the pro-resolving lipid mediator Resolvin-D1 (RvD1) early after reperfusion in both mouse and human transplanted hearts, and that exogenous treatment led to elevated tissue levels of RvD1. By intravital two-photon microscopy, we discovered that that pre-operative instillation of RvD1 into the donor heart or peri-operative systemic recipient RvD1 treatment reduced recruitment of neutrophils. Mechanistically, we found that RvD1 provides protection by signaling through Alx/Fpr2 on donor monocytes, which reduces their production of IL-1b, attenuating intravascular neutrophil aggregation and extravasation.  After allogeneic transplantation, peri-operative RvD1 treatment reduces myeloid cell recruitment, abrogates macrophage pro-inflammatory signaling within cardiac allografts, and significantly prolongs graft survival. This study defines the mechanistic basis of a therapeutic strategy that modulates inflammatory responses during myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury and provides a platform for the design of clinical trials.

BackgroundSickle cell disease (SCD) is a common inherited genetic disorder and contributor to global childhood mortality and morbidity, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa. Craniofacial and skeletal changes have been described in SCD, but the subtle soft-tissue facial patterns and their variation have not been quantitatively characterized using machine-learning methods.

MethodsWe analyzed 308 front-facing smartphone photographs from 154 participants with electrophoresis-confirmed SCD and 154 age- and sex-matched controls aged from 5 months to 19 years recruited in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Predefined geometric and texture-based facial descriptors were extracted from standardized images using manually annotated landmarks. An interpretable linear support vector machine with recursive feature elimination was evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation, with features ranked according to their relevance for distinguishing participants with SCD from controls. Cross-sectional age- and sex-stratified analyses evaluated variation in selected features

ResultsThe facial analysis algorithm identified eight geometric and six texture discriminative features that were significantly different between the cohorts. A combination of six geometric features contributed most consistently to internal discrimination: distance between medial and lateral canthi, angle at nasal ala, distance from nasion to philtrum, distance from medial canthi to the columella, distance from columella to the lower lip, and distance between nasal alae. The model achieved an AUROC of 0.843 [95% CI: 0.798,0.887], and an accuracy of 0.795 [95% CI: 0.750,0.840]. Between-group difference was limited in the youngest age groups and were more pronounced in several older age groups. Conclusion: These findings demonstrate preliminary evidence that SCD is associated with quantifiable morphometric patterns. External, longitudinal, and clinically characterized studies are needed to determine whether these features may serve as reproducible digital biomarkers within a broader supportive disease-assessment framework.

Author SummarySickle cell disease (SCD) is a genetic blood disorder that affects millions of people worldwide and is a major cause of illness and death in children, specifically in Sub-Saharan Africa. Previous studies have described changes in facial and craniofacial development among people with SCD but many of these changes require special assessment or medical imaging. We examined whether measurements obtained from standardized smartphone photographs could quantify facial differences associated with SCD. We collected 308 front-facing photos of children with SCD and matched healthy controls between 5 months and 19 years old. Using computer-based facial analysis, we measured a range of geometric and texture features and used interpretable machine-learning methods to determine which ones best distinguished children with SCD. The model identified a small set of geometric facial measurements that significantly differed between groups, with larger differences observed in several older age groups. The findings provide a basis for future longitudinal and externally validated studies of facial morphology as a potential digital biomarker of disease-associated change.

metadata.summary: Diabetic cardiomyopathy is a clinical condition of ventricular dysfunction, with obesity and insulin resistance as the primary risk factors. Under this condition, the heart accumulates fatty acids and encounters lipotoxicity, which impairs cardiac insulin sensitivity and leads to cardiomyopathy. Angiotensin-(1-9) is a peptide of the counter-regulatory axis of the renin-angiotensin system with cardioprotective effects in myocardial infarction. However, its role in diabetic cardiomyopathy is unknown. To explore the role of angiotensin-(1-9), we first induced lipotoxic stress in the heart by high-fat diet (HFD) feeding in mice. Angiotensin-(1-9) was then administered for four weeks using osmotic mini-pumps. Cardiac function was assessed by, and insulin sensitivity was evaluated in tissues after a bolus of insulin injection. Moreover, lipotoxic stress in vitro was modeled by high glucose medium plus palmitate in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs). We show that angiotensin-(1-9) improves myocardial function and reverts pathological cardiac remodeling in mice. Moreover, angiotensin-(1-9) enhances whole-body glucose tolerance and reduces homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). We next demonstrate that angiotensin-(1-9) increases insulin sensitivity in the heart and skeletal muscle but not in adipose tissue or the liver. Mechanistically, angiotensin-(1-9) does not affect insulin signaling in cardiomyocytes at baseline, while it significantly improves insulin action under lipotoxic stress through AT2 receptor (AT2R) and PKA. These findings demonstrate that angiotensin-(1-9) improves cardiac function under metabolic challenge and promotes insulin signaling in cardiomyocytes under lipotoxicity, which may shed light on the therapeutic exploration against diabetic cardiomyopathy.

BackgroundHeterotaxy (HTX) is characterised by abnormal left-right arrangement of the internal organs and is frequently associated with complex congenital heart disease (CHD). HTX is enriched among patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), due to impaired function of embryonic nodal cilia involved in left-right patterning. However, a subset of patients with HTX presents with mild or absent respiratory phenotypes and normal respiratory ciliary function, and the mechanisms underlying situs abnormalities in these non-PCD patients remain unclear. We aimed to compare the clinical history, respiratory ciliary structure, and ciliary function of patients with HTX with and without PCD.

MethodsRetrospective diagnostic data were analysed from 73 subjects with HTX referred to the Royal Brompton Hospital PCD Diagnostic Service between 1997 and 2024. Of these, 30 were diagnosed with PCD (HTX-PCD) and 43 did not meet the diagnostic criteria for PCD (HTX-only). Data included clinical history, high-speed video-microscopy (HSVM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of ciliary ultrastructure, PCD genotype and cardiac and thoracic/abdominal situs imaging.

ResultsAtrioventricular discordance (p = 0.0102) and midline liver position (p = 0.0377) were more frequent in the HTX-only group. TEM analysis identified extra microtubules in 24.4% of HTX-only subjects and microtubular disorganisation in 24.4%. Review of TEM data from 2,823 individuals referred for PCD assessment demonstrated that these ultrastructural abnormalities were associated with an increased prevalence of CHD (p = 0.04). Quantitative HSVM analysis demonstrated preserved or increased ciliary beat amplitude in HTX-only compared with HTX-PCD patients.

DiscussionHTX without PCD is associated with distinct laterality phenotypes and subtle respiratory ciliary abnormalities below current PCD diagnostic thresholds. These findings suggest that mild defects affecting ciliary structure and function may contribute to abnormal left-right patterning without causing classical PCD. Larger multicentre genetic and phenotypic studies are required to further define the mechanisms underlying HTX.

observations.text: The representational structure of human color perception across a vast color space remains incompletely understood. While classical studies measured numerous color pairs, these measurements compared only similar colors, and exploring the global relationships among thousands of colors has been infeasible due to the time costs of psychophysical experiments. Given these constraints, deep neural networks (DNNs) have attracted attention as a promising tool for providing proxies or predictions of human perception beyond psychophysical experiments. However, it remains unclear which DNNs possess embeddings that geometrically align with human color perception. Furthermore, it is unclear which learning paradigm enables DNNs to acquire a color representation that aligns with that of humans. Here, we systematically investigate which learning paradigm enables DNNs to produce a color representation that is structurally congruent with that of humans, with a focus on three types: self-supervised learning (SSL) that trains on images alone by image reconstruction, supervised learning (SL) that trains on images with category labels, and contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP) that trains on image-text pairs. We compared the embeddings of DNNs with the human similarity judgments of 93 colors using a rigorous unsupervised method, Gromov-Wasserstein Optimal Transport (GWOT). Our results show that, while each learning paradigm acquires color representations that strongly align with human data at the fine-item level in early layers, only CLIP sustains such a representation at the output. Furthermore, when we leveraged a key advantage of DNNs and investigated the representational structure of 4096 colors, the early layers of each learning paradigm and the output of CLIP consistently converged on their own characteristic structures. These structures present plausible predictions for the large-scale human color representation. Our work demonstrates an approach for exploring unknown territories of human perception using computational models validated in a limited empirical space, and provides predictions for future large-scale psychophysical experiments.

metadata.summary: Background: Direct reprogramming of cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) into induced cardiomyocytes (iCMs) holds promise as a therapeutic strategy for heart regeneration. Post-myocardial infarction (MI), resident quiescent CFs (QCFs) activate and differentiate into myofibroblasts (MFs) in the infarcted region that drive pathological cardiac fibrosis. Converting these injury-activated MFs into iCMs could simultaneously alleviate fibrosis and replenish lost cardiomyocytes. However, whether the marked heterogeneity of CFs in the infarcted heart—and in particular the activation of QCFs into MFs—creates an intrinsic barrier that limits the reprogramming of these injury-activated MFs remains unknown. Methods: To define the molecular basis of this heterogeneity, we purified PDGFRα⁺ cardiac fibroblasts and used Postn lineage tracing to distinguish injury-activated MFs from quiescent CFs, enabling matched comparison of their reprogramming competence and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) profiling of post-MI CF subpopulations. A targeted in vitro shRNA screen was conducted against 9 MF-enriched TFs as candidate molecular barriers for cardiac reprogramming. The lead candidate was validated in mouse MFs, QCFs, human iPSC-derived MFs, primary human cardiac fibroblasts, and in vivo using dual-recombinase-mediated lineage tracing. Mechanistic insights were gained through integrated bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq and Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag), together with functional assays including DNA-binding–deficient and domain-swap MEOX1 mutants. Results: We identified the upregulated transcription factor MEOX1—a known fibrosis determinant downstream of the key post-MI cytokines TGF-β1 and IL-1β—as the principal molecular barrier responsible for the profound reprogramming resistance of MFs. MEOX1 knockdown markedly enhanced reprogramming efficiency in both mouse and human MFs and enabled GATA4-free reprogramming combinations. This inhibition depended on MEOX1’s transcriptional activation activity, as disrupting its DNA-binding domain or fusing it to a repressor domain rescued reprogramming. Integrated scRNA-seq and CUT&Tag analyses revealed that MEOX1 binds and stabilizes a fibrotic, MF-defining transcriptional program that antagonizes the cardiogenic program, while also modulating the inflammatory response; its knockdown disrupted this fibrotic network to favor iCM fate acquisition. Using stringent dual-recombinase lineage tracing, we demonstrated that MEOX1 knockdown enables highly efficient in vivo MF-to-iCM conversion, leading to significant reductions in cardiac fibrosis and substantial improvement in cardiac function after MI. Conclusions: Our study identifies the pathological upregulation of MEOX1 as a key mechanism underlying the reprogramming resistance of post-MI MFs, in both mouse and human. Overcoming this barrier achieves unprecedented, lineage-confirmed in vivo reprogramming efficiency, thereby addressing a significant obstacle for the clinical translation of in situ reprogramming therapies. Data included in this Series comprise the original bulk RNA-seq datasets of MGTM-reprogrammed mouse cardiac fibroblasts with control or Meox1 knockdown and with control vector/GFP or MEOX1 overexpression; RNA-seq datasets from human iPSCs, iPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts, and iPSC-derived myofibroblasts; scRNA-seq datasets from MGTM-induced iCM cultures and normal or day-3 post-MI mouse hearts; MEOX1 CUT&Tag data; and the newly added three-biological-replicate bulk RNA-seq dataset comparing MGTM + shCtrl with MGTM + shMeox1 used for the revised manuscript.

Key pointsO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSIn the absence of nationwide reporting for coccidioidomycosis, can alternative data sources be integrated to enable estimates of monthly, county-level incidence across the US?

FindingsIn this cross-sectional study of 3,108 counties, the model identified 60 counties in non-reporting states with predicted incidence [≥]2 cases per 100,000 population (considered moderate to high incidence). In states with mandatory reporting outside of Arizona and California, the models predicted county-level incidence rates were, on average, 28% higher than those captured in national surveillance.

MeaningOur predictions highlight the extent of case under-ascertainment for coccidioidomycosis relative to Arizona and California, both in states with mandatory reporting and in non-reporting states.

ImportanceCoccidioidomycosis, also known as Valley fever, is a serious fungal disease caused by inhaling Coccidioides spores aerosolized from the soil. Despite rising public health concern, the distribution and incidence of coccidioidomycosis in the US remain poorly characterized as not all states are required to report cases, and case under-ascertainment is presumed to be high, particularly outside of the endemic region.

ObjectiveTo estimate monthly, county-level coccidioidomycosis incidence across the US while accounting for widespread under-ascertainment.

Design, Setting, and ParticipantsWe integrated multisource data, including human cases diagnosed in electronic health records, serological testing of dogs, and ecological and sociodemographic predictors, in a machine learning model estimating monthly, county-level coccidioidomycosis incidence. The model was trained on surveillance data from Arizona and California from 2013 to 2023, then applied to predict incidence in states across the contiguous US over the same time period.

Main Outcomes and MeasuresIncidence of coccidioidomycosis at the monthly county level.

ResultsThe model predicted coccidioidomycosis incidence from 2013 to 2023 for 3,108 counties from all states in the contiguous US. The model identified 60 counties in non-reporting states where predicted incidence was [≥]2 cases per 100,000 population (considered moderate to high incidence). In states with mandatory reporting outside of Arizona and California, the model predicted county-level incidence rates that were 28% higher (95% bootstrap interval, 0.1%-69.8%) than those captured in national surveillance, equating to a total of 608 potentially missed cases per year (95% bootstrap interval, 340-964).

Conclusions and RelevanceIn this cross-sectional study, the model quantified case under-ascertainment for coccidioidomycosis relative to Arizona and California, and highlighted the potential for alternative data sources to fill in gaps in mandatory reporting. Estimating incidence while accounting for under-ascertainment and non-reporting may help efforts to improve public and physician awareness and to detect emergence in new regions.

observations.text: During sleep and quiet wakefulness, the brain spontaneously revisits neural activity patterns associated with previous experience, a phenomenon known as reactivation, or replay. Reactivation is thought to support systems consolidation, the process by which memory retrieval becomes progressively more dependent on neocortical circuits and less dependent on the hippocampus. Importantly, reactivation is not indiscriminate: some memory traces, such as newly acquired or weakly learned ones, are preferentially reactivated. These observations have motivated the development of computational models accounting for the spontaneous reactivation of memory traces, their prioritisation for replay, and their transfer between the hippocampus and neocortex. In parallel, predictive-coding (PC) models have shown how computations attributed to hippocampal and neocortical circuits can arise from local prediction-error dynamics. Here, we connect these two lines of work by showing how autonomous intrinsic dynamics in coupled PC networks can transfer stored memory content between neural systems. The hippocampus and neocortex are modelled as two coupled PC associative memory networks, with asymmetric coupling motivated by reported interactions between hippocampal area CA1 and the prefrontal cortex. This coupling establishes a closed-loop hippocampal-neocortical dialogue in which hippocampal activity drives neocortical learning, while neocortical feedback biases subsequent hippocampal activity toward content for which neocortical support remains weak. We prove that this feedback steers hippocampal activity toward states of higher neocortical free energy, so that prioritisation emerges from the dialogue itself rather than from an explicit scheduler. In our model, neocortical learning relies exclusively on spontaneous hippocampal activity, without access to the initial training corpus. Nevertheless, we show that the neocortical network acquires correlated memory content faster than direct training on randomly sampled memory patterns. This advantage appeared for sufficiently correlated patterns, grew with their correlation, and persisted when new patterns were incrementally added during transfer. Together, these results provide a PC account in which neocortical feedback organises hippocampal reactivation to support efficient transfer of memory content during systems consolidation.

Yet, it remains unclear how well they predict cognitive functioning and to what extent their associations with cognition are reflected in brain and body measures. We applied machine learning to multimodal data from over 10,000 UK Biobank participants to evaluate the predictive value of twelve lifestyle and environment domains, spanning physical activity, diet, smoking, alcohol consumption, sleep, sexual behavior, electronic device use, and environmental exposures, for cognition, both individually and in combination, and quantified the extent to which these associations are captured by body and brain. A model integrating lifestyle and environment domains explained 23% of the variance in cognition at r=0.48, comparable to body and brain markers. Physical activity, diet, alcohol consumption, sun exposure, and local environment emerged as the strongest predictors. A composite brain marker integrating three neuroimaging modalities accounted for 57.7% of the lifestyle-cognition association, while a composite body marker spanning nine physiological systems accounted for 47.8%. Jointly, lifestyle, environment, body, and brain captured 92.6% of age-related cognitive variation. Therefore, integrating lifestyle and environmental factors enables robust prediction of cognition within the UK Biobank cohort, and much of this association is reflected in brain and bodily health. However, the generalizability of these findings to broader populations requires further evaluation.

metadata.summary: Truncating variants in desmoplakin (DSP) are a leading cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a severe heart muscle disease characterized by fibrosis and life-threatening arrhythmias. Desmoplakin anchors the junctions that hold heart muscle cells together to the internal cytoskeleton, enabling the heart to withstand the force of each contraction. No targeted therapy exists, and DSP is too large for conventional gene replacement. Here we show, in explanted human hearts and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, that truncating DSP variants reduce desmoplakin RNA and protein, and that the resulting haploinsufficiency renders cardiomyocytes vulnerable to cell–cell adhesion failure under contractile stress, preceded by disruption of the cell membrane. Lowering contractile force with the myosin inhibitor mavacamten prevents this failure. Circumventing the size of DSP, CRISPR-based transcriptional activation of the endogenous gene restores desmoplakin expression and rescues adhesion. Haploinsufficiency is therefore the primary defect in DSP cardiomyopathy, and transcriptional activation offers a therapeutic strategy.

ObjectivesTo develop and validate pixel data analysis (PDA) for reconstructing pixel-level shear-wave velocity (SWV) from saved Holder-Optimized Elastography (HOE) elastograms and to determine whether whole-field subcutaneous heterogeneity provides a quantitative signature of lymphatic obstruction compared with visual high-velocity-area (HVA) counting and sparse manual region-of-interest (ROI) sampling.

Materials and MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, 110 women after breast cancer surgery underwent lymphoscintigraphy and HOE, a pressure-minimized acquisition framework that preserves conventionally captured SWV information while additionally revealing spatial abnormalities attenuated by handheld acquisition. Reconstruction validation used 200 paired ROIs, spanning nearly the full displayed SWV range, from 49 images retrieved from the picture archiving and communication system; reproducibility was assessed across 96 matched anatomical sites from 6 participants undergoing independently reacquired HOE examinations. PDA, visual HVA counting, and manual ROI sampling were evaluated on the same HOE-acquired elastograms in task-specific common complete-case cohorts.

ResultsPDA reconstructed the machine-reported SWV with near-zero error over a range of 1.17 - 9.97 m/s (mean difference, +0.0009 m/s; mean absolute error, 0.0075 m/s; 95% limits of agreement, -0.0202 to +0.0221 m/s). For subcutaneous variance, interobserver/intraobserver intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.709/0.799 for PDA and 0.178/0.560 for manual ROI sampling. In the primary no obstruction versus partial obstruction comparison (n = 93), forearm-pooled PDA subcutaneous variance ratio yielded the highest observed area under the curve (AUC, 0.858; 95% confidence interval, 0.771 - 0.946), compared with 0.820 for visual HVA counting and 0.794 for manual ROI sampling. PDAs subcutaneous variance ratio remained a leading feature across all three comparisons (AUC, 0.858 - 0.878), including partial versus total obstruction grading, where all three frameworks showed high discrimination.

ConclusionsPDA accurately reconstructs pixel-level SWV from saved HOE elastograms and enables reproducible whole-field quantification of superficial shear-wave elastography heterogeneity. Subcutaneous variance ratio was the leading quantitative PDA feature across lymphatic-obstruction comparisons and was particularly informative in partial obstruction. The same approach also enables retrospective quantitative reanalysis of compatible archived elastograms.

Plain-Language SummaryPixel data analysis (PDA) reconstructs quantitative pixel-level shear-wave velocity from saved superficial elastography images, allowing the complete measurable color field to be analyzed rather than a few manually sampled regions. Reconstructed values closely matched machine measurements, and whole-field subcutaneous variance was substantially more reproducible than manual ROI sampling. Subcutaneous variance ratio remained a leading diagnostic signal across obstruction severities, including in partial obstruction without visually detectable high-velocity areas.

observations.text: The discrete-state model of brain dynamics has become the dominant paradigm in functional connectivity analysis, representing network activity as transitions among a fixed set of transiently recurring states while generally assuming that the states themselves do not evolve. We introduce a multilevel chronnectogram framework that relaxes this assumption and explicitly represents the higher-order temporal structure of brain dynamics, how distinct states couple and co-evolve over time, alongside the persistence of each state. The method integrates spatially guided independent component analysis (ICA) with subject-specific, state-guided dynamic ICA to capture evolving and overlapping connectivity patterns in a shared representational space. Validation on simulations with known ground truth shows recovery of continuous overlap and higher-order coupling structure invisible to discrete-state methods. Applied to resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging from the FBIRN dataset (151 schizophrenia, 160 controls), the framework reveals that the same pair of brain states is shifted toward opposite extremes across patients, with strong synchrony in some and active anti-coupling in others, creating a redistribution of connectivity regimes invisible to conventional occupancy metrics, providing a substrate in which schizophrenia can appear both hyper- and hypo-volatile depending on the measure applied.
observations.title: A Chronnectogram-ICA Framework for Tracking Continuously Evolving and Overlapping Functional Brain States

BackgroundQuantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) exhibits phase cancellation between paramagnetic (e.g. iron) and diamagnetic (e.g. myelin/protein) sources, obscuring microstructural lesion heterogeneity in multiple sclerosis (MS). We evaluated whether biophysical{chi} -separation identifies clinically meaningful lesion phenotypes and whether reduced echo sampling preserves microstructural sensitivity.

MethodsIn this cross-sectional study of 183 people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS), we analyzed 3327 quality-controlled white matter lesions using 3T MRI with a five-echo gradient-recalled echo sequence (GRE5) and a subsampled two-echo dataset (GRE2). A hybrid framework combining unsupervised clustering on whole-lesion paramagnetic ({chi}para) and diamagnetic ({chi}dia) features with rule-based compartmental edge-core gradient assignment resolved MS lesion phenotypes. Intralesional microstructural properties were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models. Multivariable linear regressions assessed associations with physical disability (Expanded Disability Status Scale, EDSS; n = 158), cognitive processing speed (Symbol Digit Modalities Test, SDMT; n = 79), and disease duration (DD; n = 161), with sensitivity models adjusting for total lesion volume, count, or DD.

ResultsThe framework identified four reproducible lesion phenotypes (Adjusted Rand Index = 0.924): Type 1 (22.7%; preserved{chi} dia), Type 2 (32.9%; high{chi} para without positive edge-core gradient), Type 3 (35.8%; attenuated{chi} dia), and Type 4 (8.6%; high{chi} para with a positive edge-core paramagnetic gradient). Higher EDSS was selectively associated with more negative signed{chi} dia within Type 4 lesions (whole: {beta} = -0.37, q = 0.020; core: {beta} = -0.37, q = 0.006; edge: {beta} = -0.34, q = 0.030) and Type 2 edge ({beta} = -0.33, q = 0.044). Type 4 core associations remained robust across sensitivity models adjusting for total lesion volume ({beta} = -0.35, q = 0.004), total lesion count ({beta} = -0.37, q = 0.008), and DD ({beta} = -0.32, q = 0.033). Abbreviated GRE2 attenuated Type 4 compartmental associations to non-significance (all q greater than 0.05; core: {beta} = -0.20, q = 0.215).

ConclusionsQuantitative{chi} -separation identified four internally stable susceptibility-defined MS lesion phenotypes, revealing disability-associated tissue heterogeneity beyond total lesion burden. Higher EDSS was associated with more negative diamagnetic measures within Type 4 cores after adjustment for lesion burden, pointing toward complex intralesional non-myelin tissue remodeling or reactive astrogliosis. Two-echo subsampling may influence compartment-specific clinical associations. By uncoupling susceptibility sources,{chi} -separation provides a quantitative framework for characterizing disability-associated lesion heterogeneity.
